mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of lines are parallel?

options.A: Two lines that intersect at a right angle
options.B: Two lines that meet at a point
options.C: Two lines that never meet and are always the same distance apart
options.D: Two lines that cross each other twice

mcqs.answer: Two lines that never meet and are always the same distance apart
mcqs.explanation: Parallel lines are defined as lines in the same plane that never intersect and stay the same distance apart. Option C describes this correctly. Options A and B describe intersecting lines, and D is impossible for straight lines.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that parallel lines remain equally separated
mcqs.question: If two parallel lines are drawn on a sheet of paper, what can be said about the distance between them as you move along the lines?
mcqs.explanation: By definition, parallel lines stay the same distance apart at every point. Therefore the distance does not change, making option C correct. Options A, B, and D contradict the definition of parallelism.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in geometric figures
mcqs.question: In a rectangle, which sides are parallel to each other?

options.B: Only the opposite sides are parallel
options.C: Only the adjacent sides are parallel

mcqs.answer: Only the opposite sides are parallel
mcqs.explanation: A rectangle has opposite sides that are parallel and equal in length, while adjacent sides meet at right angles. Hence option B is correct. Option A is false because adjacent sides are not parallel; C and D are incorrect for the same reason.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify examples of parallel lines in everyday objects
mcqs.question: Which of the following is an everyday example of parallel lines?

options.A: The edges of an open book
options.B: The two rails of a railway track
options.D: The spokes of a bicycle wheel

mcqs.answer: The two rails of a railway track
mcqs.explanation: Railway tracks consist of two long metal rails that run side by side without meeting, staying the same distance apart – a classic example of parallel lines. The edges of an open book meet at the spine (not parallel), triangle sides intersect, and wheel spokes converge at the hub.

mcqs.learning_point: Distinguish parallel lines from intersecting lines
mcqs.question: Which picture correctly shows a pair of intersecting lines rather than parallel lines?

options.A: Two lines that never meet, drawn side by side
options.B: Two lines that cross each other at a point
options.C: Two lines that are exactly on top of each other
options.D: Two lines that are curved and never touch

mcqs.answer: Two lines that cross each other at a point
mcqs.explanation: Intersecting lines meet at a point; option B depicts this. Option A shows parallel lines, C represents the same line (coincident), and D describes non‑intersecting curves, none of which are intersecting straight lines.

mcqs.question: A student draws two lines on a notebook such that the distance between them is 2 cm at the top of the page and also 2 cm at the bottom. Which statement is true?

options.A: The lines are parallel because the distance is constant
options.B: The lines are intersecting because they are on a notebook
options.C: The lines are perpendicular because the distance is measured
options.D: The lines are coincident because they have the same length

mcqs.answer: The lines are parallel because the distance is constant
mcqs.explanation: A constant distance between two lines at all points indicates they are parallel. Options B, C, and D misinterpret the situation; intersecting lines would meet, perpendicular lines meet at right angles, and coincident lines are the same line.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that parallel lines remain equally separated
mcqs.question: A student claims that two parallel lines will eventually meet if they are extended far enough. Which response corrects this misconception?

options.A: Parallel lines are only parallel on a small portion of the page
options.B: Parallel lines are defined to never intersect, no matter how far they are extended
options.C: If you draw them long enough they become intersecting lines
options.D: Parallel lines will meet at infinity, which is why they are called parallel

mcqs.answer: Parallel lines are defined to never intersect, no matter how far they are extended
mcqs.explanation: By definition, parallel lines never meet, regardless of length. Option B states the correct definition. Options A and C are false, and D introduces the incorrect concept of meeting at infinity, which is not part of the 7th‑grade definition.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise parallel lines in geometric figures
mcqs.question: In a diagram of a regular hexagon, which pairs of sides are parallel?

options.A: Each side is parallel to the side directly opposite it
options.B: No sides are parallel in a hexagon
options.C: Only the adjacent sides are parallel
options.D: All six sides are parallel to each other

mcqs.answer: Each side is parallel to the side directly opposite it
mcqs.explanation: A regular hexagon has opposite sides that never meet and are equal in length, making them parallel. Thus option A is correct. Option B is false because opposite sides are parallel; C is wrong because adjacent sides meet at vertices; D is impossible because a line cannot be parallel to multiple different directions.
